outputs.headline: False: 5G towers do not spread coronavirus
outputs.summary: There is no scientific evidence that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus or cause an increase in cases.
outputs.what_post_claims: The post claims that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, and that cases rose in areas where 5G was installed.
outputs.what_is_true: There is no scientific evidence linking 5G mobile technology to the coronavirus. COVID-19 is a disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which is transmitted between people, not through radio waves.
evidence_against: AP News rated as false the claim that maps show a correlation between confirmed COVID-19 cases and where 5G wireless service has been installed.
AFP Fact Check rated as false the claim that coronavirus is a result of 5G.
Full Fact states there is no evidence that 5G WiFi networks are linked to the new coronavirus.
outputs.sources_spoken: according to AP News, AFP Fact Check, and Full Fact
outputs.audio_script: The post claims that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, and that cases rose in areas where 5G was installed. This is false. There is no scientific evidence linking 5G mobile technology to the coronavirus. COVID-19 is a disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which is transmitted between people, not through radio waves. We are very sure of this. This information comes from fact-checks by AP News, AFP Fact Check, and Full Fact.
card_lines: False: 5G towers do not spread coronavirus
The post claims 5G towers spread coronavirus.
COVID-19 is transmitted between people, not by radio waves.
